question: Which of your two 'systems' is doing most of your thinking right now?
answer: System 1: fast, automatic, always on. It reads these words, hears anger in a voice, answers 2 + 2 unasked. System 2, slow and effortful, steps in for 17 × 24 and mostly signs off what System 1 proposes. The trouble is less that System 1 errs than that System 2 rarely notices.
move: Most of your thinking is done before you decide to think.
simply: Imagine a quick, chatty driver and a careful, sleepy navigator. The driver steers almost all the time; the navigator only looks at the map when something feels odd.
why: It explains why being smart does not stop you being fooled: the careful part of you has to be called in, and usually is not.

book.title: Thinking, Fast and Slow
book.author: Daniel Kahneman
